questions.q: PRC stands for?
questions.n: This is the official name of the national agency regulating all professions.

questions.q: What is the law that created the Professional Regulation Commission (PRC)?
questions.n: Presidential Decree 223 is the founding law of the commission.

questions.q: RA 9266, known as 'An Act to Regulate the Practice of Architecture in the Philippines,' was signed and sealed on?
questions.n: This is the official enactment date of the current Architecture Act.

questions.q: What do you call Working Drawings, Specifications, Estimates, and General Conditions?
questions.n: These collectively form the legal set of documents for the project contract.

questions.q: What is the difference between RA 545 and RA 9266 in terms of architectural practice?
questions.n: RA 9266 explicitly introduced this technical scope for architects.

questions.q: What is now allowed by RA 9266 which was not allowed in RA 545?
questions.n: RA 9266 allowed for the registration of architectural corporations/firms.

questions.q: Plans, models, and perspectives are?
questions.n: The law classifies these as the intellectual property and tools of the architect.

questions.q: An architect refuses to give the original plan to the Owner. Why?
o: The Owner is entitled only to the blueprint
The architect's work is covered by intellectual property rights/law
In order to prevent the Owner from making duplicates and/or constructing without his knowledge
questions.n: These reasons combined justify the architect's retention of original documents.

questions.q: You had a residential project for a Client. After construction, you found out the Client used your design for another project without your consent. What will you do?
o: File a case with the PRC
questions.n: Per your correction, informing the Mayor or OBO is the practical step for immediate intervention.

questions.q: A plan is drawn by a company draftsman under the supervision of a Registered and Licensed Architect (RLA). Who owns the document?
questions.n: Without the RLA's signature/seal, the work belongs to the employing entity.

questions.q: Before submitting sketches to a client, what must the architect first do?
questions.n: A formal agreement must exist before services like sketching are rendered.

questions.q: What do you call a signed proposal?
questions.n: A signed and accepted proposal is a legally binding contract.

questions.q: A person found preparing architectural plans without the necessary license or using another's seal/name is guilty of what?
questions.n: Practicing without a license is a criminal offense defined as illegal practice.

questions.q: The PRC will not issue the Certificate of Registration to a successful examinee if he commits:
o: Sign his signature in a project that he didn't design
Unethical practice by competing with other architect
questions.n: Acts of fraud during the exam or registration are grounds for refusal.

questions.q: This is NOT a reason for refusal of registration or removal from the Roster of Architects:
questions.n: Political offenses usually do not disqualify a professional license.

questions.q: After an expiration of how many years from the date of revocation can the validity of a certificate be reinstated?
questions.n: RA 9266 allows for reinstatement after a two-year waiting period.

questions.q: What is the requirement needed for a lost PRC ID?
o: Letter of request addressed to PRBOA
questions.n: This is the mandatory legal statement needed for ID replacement.

questions.q: How long will you wait for your replacement ID?
questions.n: According to your data, the PRC issues the replacement immediately.

questions.q: An architect puts up a firm with an interior designer and a civil engineer. How many percent of shares should the architect take?
questions.n: RA 9266 requires architects to hold 75% ownership in multi-discipline firms.

questions.q: Where is a 'single proprietorship' firm registered?
questions.n: Single proprietors use DTI for the name and PRC for the profession.

questions.q: Who provides Continuing Professional Development (CPD)?
questions.n: The integrated professional organization is the primary provider of CPD.

questions.q: In what condition is a Japanese student allowed to take the board exam?
o: His high school curriculum should be checked
He cannot take the exam since he is not a Filipino citizen
He should at least stayed for ten years in the Philippines
questions.n: Foreigners can take the exam if there is a reciprocity agreement between nations.

questions.q: Who is responsible for the implementation of RA 9266?
questions.n: The PRBOA is the government body that enforces the Architecture Act.

questions.q: A government architect earning P450,000.00/year designs a P50M building (PF at 7%). How much additional compensation should they ask?
questions.n:
This amount is 50% of the annual salary (
450
,
000
/
2
450,000/2).

questions.q: What should a foreign boss do to practice in the Philippines?
o: He is not allowed to put up a firm
Register his firm and begin practicing
Collaborate with a Filipino Firm/Architect as partners
questions.n: Foreigners must associate with local RLAs to practice legally.

questions.q: If Juan (a local graduate) and his foreign boss become partners, where should the company be registered?
questions.n: Partnerships must register with the SEC for entity and PRC for accreditation.

questions.q: Juan passes the FLEA at Jeddah. After passing, to whom is he civilly liable for his drawings?
questions.n: According to your provided data, the liability in this scenario is 'None'.

questions.q: Who can administer the Professional Oath for FLEA passers abroad?
o: The Ambassador of the Philippines Embassy
questions.n: Ambassadors have the legal power to administer oaths in foreign posts.

questions.q: What is the liability of a concept architect on a big scale project?
o: He has civil and administrative liability
They all share the same amount
questions.n: Per your correction, the non-signing concept architect is not liable.

questions.q: Under SPP Document 202, what percentage of the Architect's Fee is due upon the completion of the Schematic Design Phase?
questions.n: The schedule of payments mandates that a total of 15% of the fee is reached at the end of the Schematic Design phase.

questions.q: Which document contains the 'Architect’s Credo' and the 'Code of Ethical Conduct'?
questions.n: The Credo is the preamble to the formal Code of Ethical Conduct for Filipino Architects.

questions.q: A client asks you to perform a 'Feasibility Study' for a potential shopping mall. Under which SPP document does this service fall?
questions.n: Pre-design services, including feasibility and site selection, are covered under Document 201.

questions.q: In the Architect's responsibilities, to whom does the architect owe the duty of 'professionalism and integrity' first and foremost according to the Credo?
questions.n: The architect's primary responsibility is to the public's safety, health, and welfare.

questions.q: Which phase of Regular Design Services involves the preparation of the final 'Blueprints' for building permit application?
questions.n: This phase produces the complete technical drawings and specifications required for permits and construction.

questions.q: If an architect is hired to supervise the actual construction to ensure the quality of materials and work, what is this service called?
questions.n: SPP Document 204-A covers the architect's role in full-time site supervision.

questions.q: What is the multiplier usually applied to the direct personnel expenses for calculating fees in complex projects?
questions.n: A multiplier of 1.5 to 2.5 is the standard range to cover technical work and firm overhead.

questions.q: When an Architect is asked to provide 'Expert Witness' testimony in a legal case, under which service is this classified?
questions.n: Specialized services like legal testimony or forensic architecture fall under Consulting Services (SPP 209).

questions.q: What is the maximum amount of time an architect can be imprisoned for the illegal practice of architecture under RA 9266?
questions.n: The penal provisions specify a prison term ranging from six months to six years.

questions.q: Which of the following is considered an 'Allied' profession that an architect might collaborate with under SPP 203?
questions.n: Interior Design is specifically listed as a specialized allied service in the SPP.

questions.q: Under SPP Document 202, what is the total cumulative percentage of the Architect's Fee due after the Design Development Phase is completed?
questions.n: The schedule mandates a 15% cumulative total for Schematic plus 20% for Design Development, totaling 35%.

questions.q: What is the maximum travel distance to an exit in a building without an automatic fire suppression system?
questions.n: The National Building Code generally limits travel distance to 45 meters unless a sprinkler system is installed.

questions.q: Which SPP document covers 'Post-Construction Services' such as building administration and maintenance coordination?
questions.n: Document 205 specifically handles the architect's role after the building is completed.

questions.q: According to the Fire Code (RA 9514), what is the minimum clear width of an exit door for a standard occupancy?
questions.n: A minimum clear width of 900mm (0.90m) is standard to ensure safe passage for groups and wheelchairs.

questions.q: Which type of fee calculation is most appropriate for a project where the cost of construction cannot be determined yet?
questions.n: This method bills based on actual time spent, making it ideal for undefined scopes.

questions.q: Under RA 9266, how many years of 'diversified experience' are required before a graduate can take the licensure exam?
questions.n: The law requires 2 years of diversified experience under the supervision of a mentor RLA.

questions.q: What is the occupancy classification for a building used for the gathering of 50 or more persons for purposes such as deliberation, worship, or entertainment?
questions.n: Assembly buildings for 50 or more people fall under Group H in the Building Code.

questions.q: The Architect's Code of Ethics states that an architect should not 'cut prices' to compete. This falls under the architect's responsibility to whom?
o: To his Colleagues and the Profession
questions.n: Undercutting fees is considered unfair competition and damages the profession as a whole.

questions.q: In the SPP, what is 'Comprehensive Architectural Services' (Document 206)?
o: A combination of pre-design, design, and construction services
Only specialized interior and landscape design
questions.n: Document 206 encompasses the full range of services from inception to post-construction.

questions.q: According to RA 9266, the term 'Architect-of-Record' refers to the architect who:
o: Is the most senior partner in the firm
Signs and seals the architectural plans
questions.n: The Architect-of-Record assumes full civil and professional liability by signing and sealing the documents.

questions.q: What is the minimum number of years for the term of office for a member of the PRBOA?
questions.n: Members of the Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture serve a term of 3 years.

questions.q: A ramp for the physically challenged must have a maximum slope of what, according to BP 344?
questions.n: The standard maximum slope for a ramp is 1:12 (one unit of rise for every twelve units of run).

questions.q: Which document outlines the Architect's responsibility regarding the 'Sacredness of the human life'?
questions.n: The Credo is a poetic and moral statement reflecting the architect's duty to life and the creator.

questions.q: Under RA 9266, a corporation must be registered with which body to practice architecture?
questions.n: Corporations need SEC registration for legal personality and PRC accreditation for professional practice.

questions.q: What is the penalty for any person who forces an architect to perform service without a written contract?
questions.n: RA 9266 imposes a fine of not less than P200,000 for coercing an architect into un-contracted services.

questions.q: What is the minimum height for a ceiling of a room with natural ventilation?
questions.n: The code requires 2.70m for the first floor of buildings with natural ventilation.

questions.q: Which professional is NOT allowed to sign and seal architectural plans under RA 9266?
o: Foreign Architect with a Special Permit
questions.n: Under RA 9266, the signing of architectural plans is an exclusive right of architects.

questions.q: In the schedule of payments for SPP 202, what percentage is paid at the 'Bidding or Negotiation Phase'?
questions.n: A 5% payment is typically released upon the completion of the bidding phase.

questions.q: If an architect is tasked with 'Site Selection and Analysis', under which service category does this fall?
questions.n: Site analysis occurs before the building design starts, making it a pre-design service.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of seats in a row in a place of assembly if exits are provided at both ends of the row?
questions.n: In a place of assembly, you can have up to 14 seats in a row if there are aisles on both ends.

questions.q: Which body has the power to revoke or suspend a Certificate of Registration for an architect?
questions.n: The Professional Regulatory Board of Architecture has the quasi-judicial power to discipline licensees.

questions.q: What is the minimum dimension of a kitchen, according to the Building Code?
questions.n: The Code requires a minimum area of 3.00 square meters with a minimum dimension of 1.50m for kitchens.

questions.q: What is the minimum fire resistance rating for a firewall?
questions.n: A firewall must typically have a minimum fire-resistance rating of 2 hours to prevent fire spread.

questions.q: When an architect acts as a 'Construction Manager', whose interests do they primarily represent?
questions.n: A Construction Manager is hired by the owner to protect their interests in schedule, cost, and quality.

questions.q: Under RA 9266, how much is the fine for an UNLICENSED person who practices architecture?
questions.n: The penal provisions specify a fine between P100,000 and P5 million for unlicensed practice.

questions.q: In BP 344 (Accessibility Law), what is the minimum width of a corridor?
questions.n: A minimum width of 1.20 meters is required to allow for wheelchair maneuverability.

questions.q: Which SPP document governs 'Architectural Design Competitions'?
questions.n: Document 208 specifically sets the rules for architectural competitions.

questions.q: According to the Building Code, what is the maximum height of a riser in a standard stairway?
questions.n: The National Building Code allows a maximum riser height of 200mm.

questions.q: What is the minimum distance between two exit doors in a building?
o: 1/4 of the diagonal of the building
1/2 of the diagonal of the building
questions.n: Exits must be separated by at least half the length of the building's maximum diagonal dimension.

questions.q: Which type of 'Design-Build' service involves the architect also providing the funding for the project?
questions.n: This often involves a financial commitment or 'funding' structure to ensure the price.

questions.q: Under RA 9266, an architect's civil liability for a building that collapses due to defects in the plan is valid for how many years?
questions.n: According to the Civil Code and RA 9266, the architect is liable for 15 years for structural failure.

questions.q: What is the minimum width of an aisle in a place of assembly with seats on both sides?
questions.n: The standard minimum width for a main aisle in assembly areas is 1.00m.

questions.q: Who acts as the 'Executive Officer' of the PRBOA?
questions.n: The PRC Commissioner serves as the executive officer for all professional boards.

questions.q: A 'Specialist' in acoustics or lighting works under which SPP category?
questions.n: Acoustics, lighting, and landscape are all categorized under specialized services.

questions.q: In the Building Code, 'Group A' occupancy refers to:
questions.n: Group A is the classification for single-family or two-family dwellings.

questions.q: Under the Fire Code, what is the 'Fire Safety Inspection Certificate' (FSIC)?
o: A document proving the architect has a license
A permit for the installation of gas pipes
A certificate required before an occupancy permit is issued
questions.n: The FSIC proves the building has met all fire safety requirements for its users.

questions.q: What is the maximum 'multiplier' for the Multiple of Direct Personnel Expenses (MDPE) method in complex projects?
questions.n: The standard professional multiplier range for MDPE is 1.5 to 2.5.

questions.q: What is the minimum dimension of a toilet and bath (T&B), according to the Building Code?
questions.n: The code allows a minimum of 1.20 square meters with a minimum dimension of 0.90m for T&B.

questions.q: Which SPP document governs 'Design-Build Services'?
questions.n: Document 207 specifically covers the architect's role in design-build delivery.

questions.q: The 'Architect's Fee' generally does NOT include which of the following?
questions.n: Engineering fees are typically separate from the basic architectural fee unless negotiated otherwise.

questions.q: According to the Building Code, what is the 'Total Gross Floor Area' (TGFA)?
o: The total area of the lot
Only the area used for living space
The total floor space within the building including external walls
The footprint of the building on the ground
questions.n: TGFA is the sum of all floor areas of all levels of the building.

questions.q: What is the minimum height for a handrail from the floor?
questions.n: Handrails should be positioned between 800mm and 900mm from the floor for safety.

questions.q: Under RA 9266, how is the 'Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects' (IAPOA) defined?
o: A government agency under the DPWH
The body that writes the board exam questions
The only professional organization for all architects in the PH
A union for draftsmen and architects
questions.n: IAPOA is the unified organization (currently the UAP) recognized by the PRC.

questions.q: In project management, what does 'CPM' stand for?
questions.n: CPM is a project modeling technique used to schedule and manage complex projects.

questions.q: What is the minimum fire-resistance of an exterior wall located less than 600mm from a property line?
questions.n: Exterior walls close to the property line must be firewalls with at least 2 hours of resistance.

questions.q: According to RA 9266, 'Structural Conceptualization' includes the design of which building parts?
o: The load-bearing system and its arrangement
questions.n: It encompasses the architect's vision of how the building stays upright and stable.

questions.q: What is the maximum number of storeys for a 'Wood Frame' (Type I) building according to the code?
questions.n: Type I (Wood Frame) buildings are generally limited to 2 storeys for safety.

questions.q: What happens if an architect fails to complete the required CPD points?
o: Non-renewal of the Professional ID Card
questions.n: The PRC requires proof of CPD compliance to renew the active license card.

questions.q: Which SPP document governs the Architect's 'Regular Design Services'?
questions.n: Document 202 is the core document for standard design work (SD, DD, CD).

questions.q: Under RA 9266, what is the 'Rule of 75%'?
o: The passing grade for the board exam
The amount of the fee paid after blueprints are done
Architects must own 75% of a partnership with other professionals
The percentage of architects who must be UAP members
questions.n: In a multi-discipline firm, architects must maintain 75% ownership to ensure professional control.
